title: Righteous Kings
hook: When King Asa stood before his newly purified temple, fresh from demolishing the idols his own grandmother had installed, he made a decision that would define his reign—and ultimately undo it. The Chronicler tells us Asa did what was "good and right in the eyes of the LORD," a verdict that measured him not by military victories or political alliances, but by a far more demanding standard: divine approval. For decades, this alignment held—prophets spoke, the king listened, and Judah flourished in a rare season of peace. But 2 Chronicles reveals something unsettling about even the most righteous kings: spiritual strength at the beginning of a reign offers no guarantee at its end. Asa, who once tore down altars with his own hands, would later imprison a prophet and seek physicians instead of God; Jehoshaphat, praised for seeking the LORD with all his heart, would bind his son in marriage to Ahab's daughter and nearly die in a battle God never authorized. These chapters force us to reckon with a question that transcends ancient monarchy: What does it take not just to begin well, but to finish faithfully?
